subject: DPA clarifications — controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-payments.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Olivia Zhang <olivia.z@acme-payments.com>, legal@acme-payments.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA follow-up — controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo earlier — the team found Redwood's routing and caching approach promising. Before we proceed to procurement we need a few clarifications on the DPA language and operational controls so our legal and infosec can sign off: 

1) Controller vs. Processor: In your standard DPA, can you confirm Redwood is a processor and Acme Payments is the controller for customer-provided PII? We noticed a clause that mentions "joint controller" in one appendix and want to confirm the default relationship.

2) Subprocessors: Please provide a current list of subprocessors (and your process for notification/consent). Is there an allowed substitute/in-place mechanism for high-risk subprocessors?

3) Breach notice and timelines: Our policy requires notification within 72 hours of detection for incidents involving customer PII. Your DPA states "prompt notice" — can that be aligned to 72 hours and include a preliminary incident summary and follow-up cadence?

4) Data residency and logging: We will be using the Redwood Dedicated offering for EU and US traffic. Can you confirm where logs that may contain IPs/metadata are stored, retention windows, and whether we can configure retention to our policy (30/90/365 days)? Also, do you offer the option to exclude IPs from logs or pseudonymize them?

Appreciate a concise response we can pass to legal/infosec. If easier, happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Senior Security Engineer — Acme Payments
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Olivia Zhang <olivia.z@acme-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up — controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice

Hi Samir — thanks for the note and the great questions. Quick recap and answers below; I copied our infra lead so we can confirm the technical bits.

1) Controller vs. Processor
- Short answer: Redwood operates as a Processor when customers send us data for inference. We will update the DPA appendix you flagged; the "joint controller" language is used only in a narrow context for co-developed model projects and is not used for standard Hosted/Dedicated customers.

2) Subprocessors
- We'll attach our current subprocessors list and the subprocessor policy. Redwood notifies customers via the Console and by email at least 30 days prior to onboarding new subprocessors. For substitutions classified as "high risk" we will offer a migration window and, depending on contract tier, a negotiation period.

3) Breach notice and timelines
- We can commit to 72-hour initial notification for incidents impacting customer PII. The DPA will be updated to reflect that timeline and include an initial summary, known impact, and planned remediation steps, followed by regular updates until closure.

4) Data residency and logging controls
- For Dedicated customers, we can restrict data at rest to the selected region (US/EU). Log storage defaults to the same region as the deployment but can be configured separately for export. Retention is configurable; standard options are 30/90/365 days. We also support IP pseudonymization at ingestion for logs on Dedicated deployments.

Next steps:
- I will send an updated DPA appendix, the current subprocessor list, and a short technical note from Dev confirming retention/pseudonymization controls.
- Can you confirm the Acme legal contact for the DocuSign envelope?

I can also set up a quick 30-minute call if you prefer to go through the items live.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

- Where logs are stored for Dedicated (region and default retention)
- Whether IP pseudonymization is supported at ingestion and how it's implemented (hashing/PEP)
- Subprocessor onboarding notification mechanism and whether we can add a 30-day email notice clause for Acme
- Incident response: does our detection timeline support "notification within 72 hours of detection" and what information we can guarantee in the initial summary

Thanks — we need these by EOD PT so I can send the package to Acme legal tomorrow.

Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA follow-up — controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice

Marissa / Ethan — answers below, keeping them short so legal can paste into the appendix: 

- Logs for Dedicated: stored in the customer's selected region by default (US-East, US-West, EU-West). Retention is configurable per deployment; defaults are 90 days but can be set to 30/90/365 days via the Console or API.

- IP pseudonymization: supported. We apply a one-way SHA-256 hash with a per-deployment salt at ingestion; the plain IP is not stored on the logging tier for Dedicated deployments when pseudonymization is enabled. We document the process in the technical appendix.

- Subprocessor onboarding notification: we maintain a public subprocessor list and send an automated 30-day notice to account admins via email and a Console banner. For customers on enterprise contracts we can commit to contractual notice and a 30-day negotiation window for high-risk changes.

- Incident detection/notification: our IR team aims to provide an initial incident summary within 48-72 hours of detection for incidents impacting customer PII. The initial summary includes detection time, affected services, preliminary scope, and immediate mitigations; follow-ups are provided at least every 72 hours until closure.

Let me know if you want a one-page PDF we can attach.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Hi Samir / Olivia,

Thanks for the patience — attaching the updated materials as discussed. TL;DR on the items you asked about (for your legal/infosec):

- Controller/Processor: Redwood will be the Processor for standard Hosted and Dedicated inference; appendix language referencing "joint controller" has been removed for standard customers.

- Subprocessors: attached is the current subprocessor CSV and our policy. We provide a 30-day email notice for new subprocessors and for enterprise customers can contractually commit to a 30-day negotiation/migration window for high-risk changes.

- Breach notice: Redwood will provide an initial written notification within 72 hours of detection for incidents involving customer PII. The initial notice will include detection time, affected services, preliminary scope, and remediation steps; updates will follow at least every 72 hours.

- Data residency & logs: For Dedicated, logs default to the deployment region (US/EU) and retention is configurable (30/90/365 days). IP pseudonymization is supported via SHA-256 + per-deployment salt at ingestion for Dedicated deployments when enabled.

Next steps:
- I've uploaded the DPA appendix and subprocessor list here: https://app.redwood.ai/dpa/ACME-2026-109
- Please confirm the Acme signing contact for DocuSign and whether you want the DocuSign envelope set to "sign now" or "review only" for legal.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Summary.pdf, subprocessor_list_2026-09.csv
